status: target beginner-foundation mapping; learner-facing implementation follows separately
purpose: Map the current four-course V4 free foundation into the ORIENT/SUPPORT responsibility model and define the learner/assessment correction required for Systems Thinking without promoting deeper department source nodes into free technician instruction.
foundation_outcome: A learner completing the free foundation should understand the live-production environment, know what is expected of an entry-level hand, recognize major department functions and common hazards/boundaries, support work under direction, protect other departments' work, communicate useful information, and make an informed decision about which technical direction to pursue next.

current_v4_surfaces.implementation_rule: Keep the practical task/boundary/handoff emphasis. Orientation content may lead into support behavior, but the course must not claim field experience or independent technical authority.

current_v4_surfaces.target_role: cross-department dependency awareness for a useful hand
current_v4_surfaces.canonical_identity_rule: This is a V4 presentation bundle, not a new one-to-one canonical V2 course identity.
current_v4_surfaces.paid_source_boundary: Supporting technician/deep V2 nodes remain in their own responsibility/access state. Course 02 may borrow only the recognition/context needed for free SUPPORT-level understanding; it must not flatten paid technician operation into the foundation bundle.
current_v4_surfaces.target_learning_outcome: Before moving, disconnecting, relabeling, rerouting, changing, or reporting something, understand enough about what it affects to protect the show, preserve the current state, communicate clearly, and stop/escalate when the task crosses the learner's role.

presentation_correction.problem: The current course teaches from system architecture downward and then assesses the author's abstract vocabulary. A working hand may already use the correct judgment without naturally describing it as source/path/control/destination/verification or upstream/downstream dependencies.
presentation_correction.required_direction: Teach from recognizable floor situations upward. Plain worker-facing language is primary; formal systems vocabulary may appear secondarily as optional terminology after the practical idea is clear.
presentation_correction.field_translation: Before I move or change this: what is it, where is it going, who is using it, what might depend on it, and do I actually have authority to change it?

must_measure: preserving labels, routing, documentation, and current state
handling a field-vs-document conflict by clarifying/escalating
describing symptoms and changes without pretending to know the cause
understanding that system literacy does not create technical authorization
assessment_contract.preferred_item_style: short realistic floor scenarios with plausible distractors
avoid: definition recall as the main evidence of mastery
obvious strawman distractors such as blame another department, hide damage, or make random repairs
questions that require technician-level configuration/diagnostic authority
assessment_contract.pass_rule: Retain the current end-of-course five-question, 80-percent, retry-allowed mechanics unless a separate assessment-policy decision changes it.

current_v4_surfaces.implementation_rule: Keep receiving, identification, custody, prep/QC awareness, movement/flow, and discrepancy handoff at support level. Do not turn equipment repair, powered-equipment authorization, hazardous-material handling authority, or technical servicing into implied beginner permissions.
current_v4_surfaces.assessment_status: mostly aligned; reduce formal internal jargon where plain shop language is clearer

current_v4_surfaces.target_role: transition from general hand readiness into informed specialization
current_v4_surfaces.implementation_rule: Teach what departments actually do, what support work looks like, what problems each department owns, and which deeper technician paths exist. Do not make the learner memorize Crew Blueprint taxonomy as if it were job competence.
current_v4_surfaces.assessment_status: needs construct review; current items partly test internal career taxonomy rather than useful work understanding

recommended_zero_knowledge_flow.learner_question: What is this industry and what is happening around me?
How do I become useful without getting ahead of my role?
How does my task affect other people and systems on the show?
Which department or technical problem do I want to learn next?
What do I need to understand to take technician-level responsibility in that department?
surface_sources: department technician pathways after reviewed SUPPORT-to-OPERATE thresholds

foundation_invariants: No free foundation assessment may imply that passing establishes field experience, job qualification, certification, employer authorization, or practical competency.
Safety awareness needed for recognition, stop-work, role boundaries, or escalation remains reachable before paid technician depth.
Department-specific source nodes may support a foundation presentation without changing their own canonical responsibility/access classification.
The learner-facing sequence may synthesize several V2 identities, but lineage remains explicit in the integration graph.
A zero-knowledge learner should not be forced to choose a department before receiving enough industry and hand-level context to make the choice meaningfully.
next_actions: Rewrite the Systems Thinking learner-facing presentation from floor situations upward while preserving the same bounded competencies.
Replace the current Systems Thinking phrase-recall assessment bank with scenario-based SUPPORT-level items.
Audit Department Explorer assessment construct separately.
Create department SUPPORT-to-OPERATE threshold maps before paid entitlement implementation.
Do not activate paywall delivery until the learner graph consumes reviewed responsibility/access classifications.
